Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female university student presenting with urinary symptoms including dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic pain, and recent hematuria, suggestive of urinary tract infection; treatment plan initiated, urine sample arranged, and safety-netting advised.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Burning/stinging pain on urination, increased urinary frequency, and suprapubic (lower abdominal) aching pain primarily during urination.
- Timeline: Symptoms have been present for just under one week; have not occurred previously.
- Urine noted to be pink today, possibly with blood for the first time.
- No pain radiating to the back or sides.
- No nausea, vomiting, fevers, or unexplained systemic symptoms.
- Bowel history: Chronic variable bowel habits, attributed to pre-existing IBS, but no new or worsening GI symptoms.
- Denies unusual vaginal discharge.
- Last menstrual period: Two weeks ago.
- Sexual history: Sexually active with long-term boyfriend, combined oral contraceptive pill; no condom use; last unprotected sex approximately 1–2 weeks ago.
- Recent history of single cannabis use (first time) at a party 1.5 weeks ago.
- Denies regular smoking or drug use; drinks alcohol occasionally/socially.
- Eating and drinking well.
- No known family history of bladder or kidney problems.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS): Variable bowel movements; no current/worsened symptoms.
- No other medical conditions stated.
- Allergies: Clindamycin (reported adverse reaction).
- Medications:
  - Combined oral contraceptive pill (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Mebeverine (for IBS; dose/route/frequency not documented).

Social History:
- University student studying English; started course a few months ago.
- Lives in university halls with flatmate; family lives just outside London and is well.
- Occasional/social alcohol use.
- First use of cannabis (weed) 1.5 weeks ago at a party; not planning to use again; does not smoke tobacco.

Family History:
- No family history of bladder or kidney problems; no other relevant family history noted.

Physical Examination:
- No examination performed; no vital signs documented.

Investigations:
- Urine sample to be provided for analysis (both on-site dipstick and laboratory testing planned).
- No other investigations or test results documented.

Assessment & Plan:

- Issue 1: Suspected Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infection (UTI)/Cystitis
  - Assessment: Dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic pain, and new-onset hematuria, in otherwise healthy 19-year-old female with no systemic features or complications.
  - Plan:
    - Empirical antibiotic therapy offered: Choice of Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin (antibiotic and regimen not specified; dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Obtain mid-stream urine sample for dipstick and laboratory analysis.
    - Advise increased oral fluid intake to ensure adequate hydration.
    - Advise paracetamol as needed for pain (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Safety-net: Return promptly if develops fever, back pain, vomiting, or if symptoms persist/worsen over the next week.
    - Follow-up plan: Clinic will contact patient with urine test results; if no improvement, advised to reattend.
- Issue 2: IBS (background)
  - Stable; no changes to management.
- Issue 3: Recent cannabis use
  - Not felt to be related to current symptoms; discouraged further use.

General plan items if applicable:
- None documented beyond above.

Quality checks (document_quality):

●	Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs or physical examination performed/documented.
  - No urine dipstick results available at time of consult.
  - Specific details regarding antibiotic selection and dosing not documented.
  - No confirmation of pregnancy testing despite recent unprotected sex, though low suspicion based on regular pill use and normal period; pregnancy not formally excluded.
  - Allergies, medication names confirmed, but doses/routes/frequencies not specified.
  - No documentation of renal function or further STI assessment, though not directly indicated from history.
●	Internal conflicts: None noted.
●	Transcript quality: Clear and comprehensive; all major symptoms elicited. Minor conversational interruptions, but all key data elements reported.
